_comment: The single source for every number shown to a reader. docs/documentation-plan.md §3: figures render from an artifact, never from typed prose, and each carries the date and sample size it was measured with. docs/measurements.md is the narrative version of this file; the in-app 'How it works' panels read this one. Regenerate from arena/ladder.py and bench/benchmark.py rather than editing by hand.
conditions: double rounds, paired t-test, agents bidding for trump; EVAL rules (Weis, Stöck and the match bonus off) up to measurements.md §5k, HOUSE rules for most later results

ladder.engine: ISMCTS, no endgame solver — re-taken after measurements.md §3e
ladder.note: Rule-based trump selection for all agents, so these compare card play only. `arena/ladder.py` now *enforces* that: RandomAgent's own default is to bid at random, which made every rung above it a measurement of bidding too, and contradicted this note. The figures recorded before 2026-09-14 were taken on the voting search with the endgame solver in and do not reconcile with independently replicated deltas — they are not carried forward.

trump_selection.note: Identical card play on both sides; only the bidding differs.

conventions.note: Table conventions on against off, identical search budget both sides. They only re-order moves the search rated the same, so what is being tested is that they cost nothing — not that they gain.

convention_price.note: The researched Swiss conventions may choose any move within 0.01 of a round's share of the best, by the search's own estimate. Against conventions off at the shipped budget: free. 'predictable' is the share of the decisions a convention speaks to in which the bot plays the convention's card, offline on saved decisions. A price of 0.02 reached 79.7% and cost 0.5 (49.49%, p = 0.018). measurements.md §5u.

signal_reading.note: Reading the discard convention into the determinization prior. Two nulls and one borderline p=0.049 that did not replicate; reported as a null and off by default. See measurements.md §5c.

game_objective.note: Projecting the round onto the game instead of maximising the round's share. Whole games, paired, HOUSE rules — arena/games.py, because the round-level instrument cannot see this and would score it backwards. Three versions; the first two lost, the third is harmless. See measurements.md §5d.

bidding_prior.note: Reading the bidding into the imagined hands — the strongest prior available, and null. measurements.md §5e has the mechanism: a prior only flips decisions the search already rates within 0.008 of each other.

adversarial_search.note: Modelling the other team as opponents. The tree maximised the root team's value at every node, including theirs, so it valued lines by what happens when the opposition cooperates. A correctness fix; pooled +0.30% +/- 0.32 over n=1800, never significant.

split_sweep.note: How a fixed budget is split between determinizations and iterations, endgame solver off. An inverted U with a broad flat top: at least ~10 worlds and ~30 iterations each, and within that nothing matters. Closes the 'allocation guidance' explanation in measurements.md §3.

risk_aversion.note: Concave kink in the reward to offset determinized search's optimism. All null, drifting slightly negative. An affine penalty would have been provably a no-op; see measurements.md §5f.

leaf_evaluator.note: Phase 0 of value-net-plan.md: a linear evaluator fitted to the random playout's own mean. Nine points worse at every split. The playout's error is zero-mean and washes out across 2400 samples to ~0.019; the evaluator's is bias at 0.232 and never washes out. Kill criterion fired. See measurements.md §5g.

ismcts.note: Information Set MCTS: one tree shared across every imagined world instead of a tree per world and a vote. The first change in this file to make the bot stronger. Replicated three times. See measurements.md §5h.

resample_every.note: Iterations sharing one imagined world. The gain is intact at 4 and gone at 8 — a cliff, not a slope. Shipped default 4: full advantage at 1.41x the determinized search rather than 1.95x.

fusion.note: The gap to a bot that sees all four hands, endgame solver off. It narrows by 0.74 of ~9 points, so strategy fusion is real and is about 8% of what hidden information costs.

policy_prior.note: Hand-written best-play knowledge in the selection rule rather than the reward, so it steers the search without biasing the value. Ordering null; the PUCT hump at c=1 was the best of five comparisons and did not replicate; c=4 is significantly worse, which proves the prior is active and wrong. Same lesson as greedy==random. See measurements.md §5i.

learned_prior.note: A policy distilled from 40,190 of the search's own decisions, in the same slot as the hand-written prior of §5i. 48% top-1 agreement, and it recovers the Swiss conventions from self-play — but null in play, did not replicate, and a uniform-prior control is null too. Structural reason: 4.2 legal moves and 2,400 iterations means ~571 visits per candidate, so there is nothing for a prior to prune. See measurements.md §5j.

belief_value.note: With probability p the search imagines the true deal. Concave: a fifth of the information buys a third of the cheating gap, and the return per unit peaks near p=0.1-0.2. Beliefs are the largest lever measured in this file. Upper bound only — injecting truth is stronger than any inference. See measurements.md §5k.
belief_value.bar: ~0.07-0.13 points per 1% of oracle-equivalent accuracy, so beating ISMCTS's +1.15 needs inference worth ~10% of an oracle.

shown_weis.note: The winning Weis is turned face up to prove it, and the search was dealing those cards to random seats. Now pinned as hard constraints. Invisible to every other figure in this file because EVAL switches Weis off. See measurements.md §5l.
shown_weis.verdict: +0.62 +/- 0.18 of a round's card points, +1.78 +/- 1.13 of games. The second measured gain in the file, and larger than ISMCTS's +1.15.

called_weis.note: The Weis values every seat calls in the first trick, including the silences — the half of the announcement protocol the search ignored. A value names no card, so it filters imagined worlds instead of forbidding cards. Building it uncovered a bug in determinize that had been discarding most of the shown-Weis pins since they landed. See measurements.md §5m.
called_weis.verdict: +0.40 +/- 0.08 of a round's share and +1.40 +/- 0.44 of games at a fixed budget; null at equal wall-clock, which is not the binding constraint at 4 ms a move. The sampler fix it uncovered matters more than the feature.

budget_sweep.note: Measured on the voting search that §5h replaced. Each budget played against a fixed 2,400-iteration reference, endgame solver off. On the shared tree the budget keeps paying — see budget_under_house.

budget_under_house.note: §3's saturation does not hold for today's engine. The budget keeps paying to 64x and is flat after it, under HOUSE and under EVAL alike — so the Weis constraints are not the explanation, and §3 is not condition-dependent. The candidate that fits is that §3 measured the voting search that §5h replaced, and its number was carried across the change without being re-taken. Each row is pooled over independent seeds against the same 2,400-iteration reference. See measurements.md §3b.

pimc_control.note: The voting search §5h replaced, same conditions and budgets. Flat — so §3's saturation was a property of that algorithm, not of the engine.

budget_under_house.verdict: +0.56 of a round's share at 64x under HOUSE, +0.70 under EVAL. 256x buys at most +0.08 more, inside its own noise, for 4.7x the time — so 153,600 is the top of the curve rather than the limit of patience.

levers_at_the_new_budget.note: Constants set when a move had to cost milliseconds, re-asked at 153,600 iterations. Both survive. See measurements.md §3c.

rows.note: A loss, not a null. An exact solve is perfect information inside a world that is mostly wrong; deepening it sharpens the per-world answers and worsens the fusion between them. See measurements.md §3d.

endgame_depth.note: How deep the exact solver should take over from ISMCTS. Monotone: less is better, and none is best. A solve is perfect information inside one imagined world, so voting between several of them is the strategy fusion the shared tree exists to avoid. See measurements.md §3e.
endgame_depth.verdict: +1.71 of a round's share, the largest gain in this file, at every budget tried. A deletion rather than a feature.

post_ismcts_recheck.note: Pre-§5h results re-run against today's engine — shared tree, no endgame solver, 153,600 iterations. See measurements.md §3f.

cheating_gap.note: Not comparable with the ladder in §4: different engine on both sides and a different budget. Restating §4 needs its whole ladder re-run.

throughput.note: Search budget 2,400 iterations, kept as the like-for-like benchmark. It was taken as the saturation point until measurements.md §3b; the bots have searched 153,600 since.

endgame.status: OFF by default since measurements.md §3e — turning it off is worth +1.71 of a round's share (n=4000). The costs below are what it *would* cost, kept because the solver is still correct for a search that votes.
endgame.note: Exact double-dummy solve, median nodes visited. Roughly 15x per extra card, which is why the solver replaces the search rather than running at every leaf.

literature.human_parity: 49.5% ± 14.2% of points, six experienced human teams over 136 rounds, against a DMCTS team
literature.trump_selection_claim: ~16 points of win rate over choosing at random

trump_fit.engine: ISMCTS, 2,400 iterations for the labels; card play at 2,400 for the games
trump_fit.note: measurements.md §5n. Contracts priced by simulation (arena/contracts.py, 3,000 hands x 16 deals), weights fitted on half the hands (arena/fit_trump.py). Values are game points: RoundScore.total already carries the multiplier — a first pass that multiplied again was discarded.

play_model.note: measurements.md §5o. rust/src/playmodel.rs: 36 features, 32 hidden units, trained on the shipped search's own play at 38,400 iterations.

belief_offline.note: measurements.md §5o. Oracle-equivalent p = (a - u)/(1 - u) on the axis of belief_value. Pool 2,048, 1,500 decisions.

play_model_in_search.note: measurements.md §5p. Equal iterations, then equal time against the shipped 153,600. Neither ships.

exploration.note: measurements.md §5p. HOUSE, 153,600 iterations, against the shipped 1.5.

belief_network.note: measurements.md §5q. Oracle-equivalent p on the 1,500 decisions of belief_offline. Null in play (2,000 deals); off.

belief_round_two.note: measurements.md §5r. Round two of the belief work: settings swept offline, the play model retrained on today's bot, trump re-priced by a labeller that reads the table.

trump_repriced.labeller: 2,400 iterations with the play likelihood on

belief_round_two.lesson: Oracle-equivalent p predicted the first belief step (+1.31, twice) and has predicted nothing since: +0.031 and +0.034 more both measured null in play.
